title: Meta hands BlackRock 80% of a $14B El Paso AI data center — and keeps it as tenant
subtitle: A joint venture will own the 1 GW Northeast El Paso campus; Meta will lease the whole thing back, financed by $12.5B in BlackRock-led debt.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Meta and BlackRock announced on July 28 a strategic joint venture to own the AI data center campus Meta is building in Northeast El Paso. BlackRock-managed funds will hold 80% of the venture and Meta will hold 20%. Meta contributes the land and construction-in-progress worth about $2.3 billion; BlackRock contributes roughly $4.9 billion in cash. BlackRock also lined up $12.5 billion in debt financing to bring the total project cost to about $14 billion. Meta will lease the entire campus back and remain the sole tenant. The site is designed for 1 gigawatt of compute capacity, with first power scheduled for 2028.

The structure is what matters. Meta is not selling the campus and it is not building it alone — it is moving the capital cost off its own balance sheet while keeping operational control as the tenant. That lets Meta expand compute footprint without pulling the full $14 billion out of a capex line it has already raised to $125–$145 billion for 2026 alone. BlackRock, on the other side, gets exposure to hyperscaler-grade AI infrastructure with a locked-in anchor tenant — a stable long-duration asset for insurance and pension-adjacent portfolios.

The deal is the latest instance of a pattern taking hold across the frontier labs: infrastructure is being financed through structured vehicles with debt, private equity, and institutional partners rather than paid for entirely out of tech-company cash flow. Oracle carries a $638 billion order backlog largely from AI. Alphabet raised its 2026 capex guidance to $205 billion. Meta's Louisiana Hyperion project alone is projected at $50 billion. The 2028 online date for El Paso says something about how compute buildouts are actually paced — the announcement is now, the electrons are two years away.

For learners: understand that AI capex has become a distinct asset class. When you read headlines about "$14 billion data centers," the operator is often not the owner, the money is largely borrowed, and the timeline is measured in years. If you are building career skills around AI, the plumbing side — power, cooling, networking, real-estate financing — is a real and growing part of the industry, and it is where a lot of the money is actually being deployed.
